requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg confirms 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' with audit_enabled=1, res=1, directly observed after a real reboot (new boot_id).

requirements.requirement: audit=1 setting is persistent and survives reboots
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot baseline (boot_id e8afb731..., cmdline without audit=1) was captured, a real reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node came back with a different boot_id (9c08d859...), post-reboot cmdline/dmesg show audit=1 active, and /etc/default/grub still contains GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" after the reboot, confirming the config drives boot behavior rather than a one-off runtime setting.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol observed for every managed node (node1)
requirements.summary: For the sole managed node, pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot identity, and recovered state (systemctl is-system-running 'running', no failed services, package health nominal, audit subsystem enabled) are all directly captured and cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare/after-executor snapshots, which show the same boot-id transition (e8afb731... -> 9c08d859...) and no failed-services or package-health regressions.

overall_summary: The executor persistently configured audit=1 via the correct (non-shadowed) GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX variable after discovering that the cloud-image grub drop-in overrides GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT, then directly verified the setting survives a real reboot: pre-reboot baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-reboot kernel cmdline/dmesg/config all confirm audit=1 is active and persistent. The sole troubleshooting misstep (editing the shadowed variable and regenerating grub.cfg prematurely) was fully corrected within the same attempt and left no residue.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; longer-term persistence (e.g., across a second reboot or kernel update) is not directly evidenced, though the persisted /etc/default/grub content and grub.cfg regeneration make it highly likely.
No dedicated diff of full package/service state beyond failed-services and package-health category checks was available, but this scope is small for a single grub-configuration change plus reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: One bounded, low-risk troubleshooting experiment occurred and was fully reverted: cmd-1ac0a6d3b7214ce7 set GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT to include audit=1 and cmd-0683c827abb04405 ran update-grub against that (incorrect, since it is shadowed by the cloud-image drop-in) configuration, temporarily regenerating grub.cfg without audit=1 actually taking effect. This was corrected by cmd-55eb4ea5303f4912, which reverted GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT back to its original 'quiet splash' value and instead set GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="audit=1" (the correct, non-shadowed variable), followed by a second update-grub (cmd-a825dddd2c874558) confirming audit=1 present in grub.cfg. No residue remains: /etc/default/grub and grub.cfg reflect only the final correct state, no failed services appeared, package health stayed 'dpkg' healthy, and temp-file/listening-socket differences between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots are attributable to normal per-boot systemd-private directories and socket owner PIDs changing across the reboot, not executor-created residue.
